historical_reviews.deepseek: The manual boundary is correct, but CCD/Core/Thread is a separate row and cannot define this row's target; an unnamed CBS write is not executable.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Classification and controls are accepted; field inventory and one explicitly approved persistence mutation are kept separate from future topology enablement coverage.
historical_reviews.history: The duplicate-code row 1572 is pending and must receive its own review; it cannot be used as this row's procedure or oracle.
historical_reviews.v3_1: AMD CBS is a menu family whose options can affect CPU, memory, interconnect, power or security behavior, so the project must name both read-only fields and exactly one safe writable checkpoint rather than authorizing an arbitrary change.

original_test_intent: Have a qualified operator verify the approved AMD CBS information matrix and demonstrate persistence for one explicitly named, reversible CBS option without importing the separate CCD/Core/Thread case.
original_method: Bind the exact SUT, BIOS and AGESA; capture the AMD CBS page and approved read-only fields; after per-step approval change only the named option from its recorded baseline to the approved test value, save/reboot/re-enter, verify persistence and dependent health, then restore and verify the baseline when required.
manual_activity: The owner names the exact CBS fields and one approved reversible option; a qualified operator performs BIOS navigation, mutation, save/re-entry, visual comparison and restoration.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/board/CPU, BIOS and AGESA identity
One exact writable option, baseline, test value and rollback value
Known dependencies and expected boot/OS effects
Recovery path for boot or access failure
safety_requirements: Never interpret `change any setting` as permission for an arbitrary CBS write
Do not borrow CCD/Core/Thread targets from row 1572
Obtain explicit approval before the named write, save and reboot
Record baseline and dependency state before mutation
Do not clear dmesg, syslog or SEL
Stop on hidden dependency change, warning, boot failure or lost console
Do not automatically retry or reset defaults
Restore only through the approved recovery path and verify final state
agent_execution_scope: Provide read-only supporting identity/health collection if requested
Coordinate but do not claim BIOS UI control
Record operator-supplied exact fields and before/after evidence
Compare values only under the approved platform specification
Track boot and dependency evidence after save/re-entry
Report discrepancies and recovery status without verdict
engineer_actions: Name fields, exact writable option, values, dependencies and acceptance criteria
Approve each BIOS mutation/reboot and recovery plan
Resolve unexpected option behavior and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its NO/manual conclusion fits, but it wrongly folds CCD/Core/Thread into this row and does not constrain the source's arbitrary-setting instruction.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Manual operator: capture the approved AMD CBS fields, change only the specifically authorized option, save/reboot/re-enter, verify persistence and dependent health, then restore/verify baseline if required.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: AMD CBS menu, information check, one setting persistence checkpoint and 5/5-minute estimates remain; the unnamed setting is converted into a required owner input rather than guessed.

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL FIELD-BOUND AMD CBS PERSISTENCE CHECK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an evidence tuple of exact menu path, field name, baseline/test/restore values, dependency snapshot, before/save/re-entry/restore captures and boot-health result.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces arbitrary mutation with one approved reversible checkpoint and explicitly isolates the duplicate-code CCD/Core/Thread case.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A successful save for one option cannot validate all CBS settings; the owner-defined read-only matrix and mutation checkpoint are reported separately.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: CBS dependencies can be platform/AGESA-specific and may change CPU topology, memory training, interconnect, security or performance.

project_override_considerations: A validated remote-console automation may assist capture, but it does not make this workflow fully automatable unless the project separately validates BIOS UI control and recovery. The row-1572 CCD/Core/Thread variant remains independent coverage.
expected_evidence: Row/variant plus SUT/CPU/BIOS/AGESA identity and approval
Owner-approved AMD CBS information and exact mutation matrix
Protected before, changed, saved/re-entered and restored BIOS captures
Named field values and dependent-setting comparison
Boot/OS/firmware health and preserved event evidence
Recovery/final-state record and engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master consistently requests AMD CBS inspection and a save/persistence demonstration. The unspecified field is a material readiness input, while CCD/Core/Thread contamination appears only in the prior AI overlay and is isolated by row/variant identity.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The case becomes safely defined when the owner names the fields, one approved reversible mutation, dependencies and recovery path; it remains MANUAL ONLY rather than irreducibly blocked.

review_improvement: Prevents arbitrary CBS mutation and duplicate-row scope leakage while requiring exact field, dependency, persistence and recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: AMD CBS is not one setting: options can alter unrelated processor, fabric, memory and power domains. Demonstrating save/persistence therefore requires a single pre-approved option with known dependencies and rollback, while the information audit remains a separately enumerated comparison against the platform matrix.
